messages.author: a18c09ce0bcb4dfb
messages.subject: Correlation between Latent Variables
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to fit a full structural equation model consisting of a measurement model and a latent variable model. The measurement model is made of three latent factor which are measured by 12 indicators. In the latent variable model, I regress two of the factors on the third factor. My data is multivariate Normal. Since I am new to Lavaan, I have tried two approaches to this end.

In the first attempt I manually define the correlations between the factors AND set orthogonal=TRUE. The syntax I am using follows:

model.sem<-'f3=~X1+X2+X3+X4
f1=~X5+X6+X7+X8
f2=~X9+X10+X11+X12
f3 ~~ f1
f3 ~~ f2
f1 ~~ f2
f1 ~~ 1*f1
f2 ~~ 1*f2
f3 ~~ 1*f3
f1=~X4
f3 ~ f1 + f2
'
model.sem.fit<-sem(model.sem,data=data,orthogonal=TRUE, estimator="ML",std.lv=TRUE,std.ov = TRUE)

After running the syntax, Lavaan warns that the model is not identified.

However, when I do not manually set the correlations and use orthogonal=FALSE the model then runs perfectly fine. The syntax follows:

model.sem<-'f3=~X1+X2+X3+X4
f1=~X5+X6+X7+X8
f2=~X9+X10+X11+X12
f1=~X4
f3 ~ f1 + f2
'

model.sem.fit<-sem(model.sem,data=data,estimator="ML",std.lv=TRUE,std.ov = TRUE)

I am still relatively new to SEM so please excuse me if I am missing the obvious.

Any help would be appreciated.

Regards,

Linniker Grech

messages.subject: Re: Correlation between Latent Variables
parts:
The reason for the error is that you define both covariances and regressions between f3 and {f1, f2}

f3 ~~ f1
f3 ~~ f2
f3 ~ f1 + f2

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Correlation between Latent Variables
parts:
isn't that what orthogonal=FALSE does? It allows the latent variables to be correlated.


Yes, that sets the default behavior, but the model syntax overrides any defaults you turn on/off (e.g., you can set std.lv = TRUE but still free some latent variances using f1 ~~ NA*f1, although that might cause identification issues). 

So in your first example, you set orthogonal = TRUE (which omitted latent covariances from the parameter table by default), but the covariances you specified in the model syntax were still then added to the parameter table anyway.  If you don't want to estimate them, leave them out of the syntax (or set them to 0 in the syntax: f1 ~~ 0*f2). 

In your second example, you didn't specify any latent covariances in your model syntax, but you left orthogonal set to its default setting (FALSE), so the covariances among your exogenous latent variables were added to the parameter table by default.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
